title: Post-merge cleanups and hypotheses
content:
Purpose:
Capture lightweight follow-ups after landing PRs (things we noted in review but intentionally left out of the main change to keep scope small). This is a personal scratchpad — aim to convert high-value items into small follow-ups (<= 1 day) or schedule for a tech-debt sprint.

Context / last landed PR: repo@main PR #2894 — async kv-cache improvements. Left several tiny items in review notes to avoid scope creep.

Quick triage rubric (how I decide if I make a follow-up PR now vs file and schedule):
- If change is mechanical and low-risk (rename, move helper, add small unit test) -> ship a follow-up PR within 24–48h.
- If change touches runtime hot path / needs perf validation -> file ticket and schedule for dedicated investigation.
- If change requires infra work (k8s config, secrets) -> file ticket and add to platform backlog.
- If change is primarily product/UX -> loop in PM and CS; do not self-attach.

Checklist for follow-up PRs (tiny ones):
- [ ] branch off main with descriptive name (postmerge/<what>-<short>)
- [ ] link original PR and mention reviewers from PR #2894
- [ ] add 1–2 line rationale in PR body (why not in original)
- [ ] add unit test or small assertion where possible
- [ ] mark as low-risk in title and add labels: small, post-merge, needs-review
- [ ] run perf sanity if touching cache/codepath (local perf smoke)

Notes and candidate follow-ups from review of PR #2894:
1) telemetry: add cache hit/miss metric around the new prefix cache wrapper
   - Hypothesis: current prefix caching reduces repeated token work, but we don't have visibility into hit-rate.
   - Quick change: add a counter with tags: model, route, prefix_len_bucket.
   - Ticket: INF-1423 (linked above). Owner: Marco can start; I can pair on metric schema.

2) tiny API ergonomics: rename param 'kvKey' -> 'prefixed_key' in internal helper to reduce confusion
   - Rationale: multiple reviewers misread kvKey as global key.
   - Risk: purely rename in internal module with grep and update tests.
   - Action: single-file change + test adapt. Time estimate: 1–2h.

3) test fragility: flakey mock for tokenizer in test_token_cache_test.go
   - Symptom: test occasionally times out under CI contention; likely race on async prewarm.
   - Quick fix: increase timeouts + add deterministic seeding OR use small sync prewarm in test only.
   - Follow-up PR: test stabilization. Time estimate: 2–4h.

4) docs: add short note in internal docs about expected prefix lengths and cache eviction policy
   - Where: docs/internal/cache.md (doesn't exist yet) or add section under infra runbooks
   - Benefit: fewer reviewer questions and faster onboarding for new SREs.

5) refactor idea: extract a tiny "CacheKeyBuilder" object to centralize prefix building and tagging
   - Trade-offs: improves testability, centralizes behavior; may add allocation overhead if done naively.
   - Experiment plan: implement as small value-type struct, benchmark with existing perf harness on 512-token median input.
   - If lightweight (<2% overhead) -> adopt. Else -> revert.

6) rollout/observability: canary rollout for new cache behavior with traffic-sampling at 5% for 24h
   - Need: route-level flag + feature gate in routing layer (product/system).
   - Owner: Delia to coordinate with platform for rollout. File ticket for rollout plan.

Open questions (to answer before follow-ups or in the next sync):
- Do we want cache hit metrics per-customer or only per-route? Cost/TSX implications.
- Should prefix_len_bucket be static (0-8,9-32,33+) or dynamic quantiles? (dynamic needs histogram buckets and more storage)
- Who owns the runbook updates for cache eviction surprises? (sre vs runtime team)

Short-term next steps (this week):
- [ ] Make rename 'kvKey'->'prefixed_key' (me) — target: 2/14
- [ ] Open PR for test stabilization (me + Marcos) — target: 2/15
- [ ] Draft INF-1423 with metric schema (Marco) — target: 2/16
- [ ] Sync with Delia about rollout requirements (15m) — target: 2/17

Timeboxing rules for me:
- If a follow-up takes >4h, convert to a ticket and schedule properly.
- Avoid scope creep: each follow-up must aim to be single-concern.

Snippets / examples (for quick copy when making PRs):
- PR title template: "post-merge: rename prefixed key helper (low risk)"
- PR body template: "This change implements a mechanical rename noted during PR #2894 review to clarify intent. No behavior change expected; updated unit tests. Links: #2894, INF-1423."

Quick grep helpers I used when inspecting the repo (so I don't forget):
- Find uses: rg "kvKey|prefix.*cache" -S 
- Tests: go test ./... -run TestTokenCache -count=1

Slack threads / context:
- convo: #eng-runtime thread starting 2025-02-10 09:12 AM (see linked message). Some follow-ups were suggested by @marco and @delia.

If I get blocked: file a small note in PR #2894 thread with a summary and ping reviewers — keeps context linked.

Longer-term ideas (capture only):
- Consider per-route adaptive cache sizing driven by learned median prefix lengths per route. Could be an Optimize feature.
- Integration test harness: run end-to-end workload with synthetic prefixes to validate eviction policy.

End note: this doc is my personal TODO buffer for small, high-value post-merge items. I will prune weekly and either close trivial ones or push into sprint planning.
